17. Four charges $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$ and $Q_4$ of same magnitude are fixed along the $x$ axis at $x = -2a$, $-a$, $+a$ and $+2a$, respectively. A positive charge $q$ is placed on the positive $y$ axis at a distance $b > 0$. Four options of the signs of these charges are given in List I. The direction of the forces on the charge $q$ is given in List II. Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists.

List I
P. $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, $Q_4$ all positive
Q. $Q_1$, $Q_2$ positive; $Q_3$, $Q_4$ negative
R. $Q_1$, $Q_4$ positive; $Q_2$, $Q_3$ negative
S. $Q_1$, $Q_3$ positive; $Q_2$, $Q_4$ negative

List II
1. $+x$
2. $-x$
3. $+y$
4. $-y$

Q2 and Q3 are negative charges, so they attract the positive charge q; likewise, because of left-right symmetry, the horizontal components cancel each other, and the vertical components are both downward. Therefore the resultant force is along the negative y direction.

method.method_draft: Use symmetry and qualitative force directions. From the diagram, pair the charges equidistant from the y-axis: Q1 at -2a with Q4 at +2a, and Q2 at -a with Q3 at +a. From the text, Q1 and Q4 are positive and q is positive, so both outer charges repel q; their horizontal components cancel and their vertical components both point upward. Q2 and Q3 are negative, so both inner charges attract q; their horizontal components cancel and their vertical components both point downward. Since the inner pair is closer to q than the outer pair and all source charges have equal magnitude, the downward attraction from Q2 and Q3 is stronger than the upward repulsion from Q1 and Q4. Therefore the net force is along -y.

method.method_draft: Compute the net force components using Coulomb's law. From the image/text, q is at (0,b), Q1 and Q4 are at x=±2a with positive charge +Q, and Q2 and Q3 are at x=±a with negative charge -Q. For each symmetric pair, the x-components cancel because the positions and charge signs are mirror-symmetric. For the y-component of the electric field at q, the outer positive pair contributes +2kQb/(4a^2+b^2)^(3/2), while the inner negative pair contributes -2kQb/(a^2+b^2)^(3/2). Since (a^2+b^2)^(3/2) is smaller than (4a^2+b^2)^(3/2), the negative inner contribution has greater magnitude. Thus E_y is negative, and because q is positive, the force on q is also in the -y direction.
